title: Anthropic steers its IPO to the top of its $70 to $78 range or higher
excerpt: Anthropic IPO set for the top of its range or above, as Amodei pitches an ‘age of miracles’ and Amazon and Google stand to own over a quarter.
content_html:
Investors in Anthropic’s share sale are being told to expect a price at the top of the $70 to $78 range or above, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on Tuesday. The deal has drawn several orders of $10bn or more, Anthony Hughes and Bailey Lipschultz reported.

Multiple sources told David Faber that the price is likely to land above the range, CNBC reported. Both outlets reported that the order book closes at 4pm in New York on Tuesday, which is 21:00 UTC. TNW has not independently verified either report.

The Anthropic IPO is set to price on Wednesday, with trading on the Nasdaq under ANT from Thursday. At $78 a share, the company would be worth about $1.4tn on a fully diluted basis, Bloomberg reported. Anthropic set its IPO terms on 10 November. By Sunday, orders had reached close to seven times the shares on offer.

Amazon and Google will own more than a quarter

Amazon and Google are set to hold nearly 15% and 14% of Anthropic’s stock after the IPO and a $26bn private placement. That is according to a filing on Tuesday, as David Morris reported for Bloomberg. Google’s stake includes 135.1m non-voting shares it agreed to buy for about $10bn in that placement.

Customers of Amazon, Google and Microsoft can buy Claude through their cloud accounts. That business brought in about 44% of Anthropic’s revenue in the first nine months of 2026, the filing shows. The filing describes the three companies this way.

“[They] simultaneously serve as our investors, customers, distribution partners, and competitors,” Anthropic wrote in the filing.

Who else is buying

Coatue’s stake is worth about $10.5bn at the target valuation, a person familiar with the matter told Rebecca Torrence of Bloomberg. The hedge fund has put $4.75bn into Anthropic, the person said, starting with $250m in 2025 at a $183bn valuation. Its latest cheque was $2bn in May, at $965bn.

Altimeter Capital aims to put $5bn into the IPO, five times as much as it has ever put into one. Founder Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday why.

“I think this is a cornerstone compounder for a long time,” Gerstner said.

Anthropic’s own staff face tighter rules. After two early windows, employees will in most cases have to sell through 10b5-1 plans, written schedules set at least 30 days ahead, Business Insider reported. Companies mostly use such plans for executives. Staff can sell 10% of their shares on IPO day, wealth adviser Teresa Greenip told Business Insider. Another 35% can go after the first quarterly report.

The risks on the table

Anthropic made $33.24bn in revenue in the nine months to 30 September, CNBC reported from the prospectus. That is up about 1,200% on a year earlier. Its net loss was $104bn, mostly from changes in the value of convertible notes and derivatives.

Its compute commitments of about $448bn through 2030 put pressure on Anthropic to keep token prices high against OpenAI, Google and others, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Mandeep Singh wrote. The prospectus also runs to 92 pages of risk factors, the Guardian noted. Jason Hollands of Bestinvest told the paper that SpaceX shares have traded below their IPO price at points since June.

In the UK, AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro are taking applications from retail investors, the Guardian reported. OpenAI’s top executives said on Monday they are not worried about Anthropic listing first.

Dario Amodei made his pitch in Anthropic’s roadshow video.

“I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia,” Amodei said.
